images.rights_note: Only source is flattened RGB object 119, cropped to source-pixel rectangle (38, 38, 1313, 1688) to reproduce the printed page. The poem, translucent reading panel and drop shadow are irreversibly baked into this sole raster; no alternate base, pieces, soft mask or transparency group exists. A crop removing the panel would discard the mountain and most of the scene, so the faithful source is retained with this explicit unavoidable-overlay exception. Separate publication/address/postage typography and vector mailing furniture omitted. No inpainting, synthesis or tonal inverse performed. No individual image credit or licence is stated in the PDF. Normalized as a baseline RGB JPEG with embedded sRGB profile and nonzero 150 dpi density; original grayscale appearance preserved where applicable. Final file visually checked against PDF and source asset; complete warning-free loads through Pillow and ffmpeg, then natural-size Skia Canvas decode/paint/readback; encoded colour space confirmed sRGB. The general masthead states “Some images © 2001-2004 www.arttoday.com”; it does not identify which images this covers, so attribution of this individual image is uncertain and no licence is inferred.

html:
When mountain walls confront the way.
Why sit and weep? Arise and say
“Be thou removed” and they shall be
By the power of God, cast into the sea.

All power on earth, all power in heaven,
To Christ the Son of God is given;
And from the throne He will endue,
And hindrances will flee from you.

O’er all the power of fiend and man
Say through the Lord, “I surely can”
Take from Him power on earth to tread,
On serpent’s sting, on dragon’s head.

Whate’er thou art, Oh mountain high,
Where’er thou art in earth or sky,
Whene’er thou art, truth is the same,
“Be thou removed in Jesus name.”

“Be thou removed” faith bids thee start
For yonder see—arise! depart!
I may, I can, I must, I will,
The purpose of my God fulfill.
